angle: CURIOSITY IN A PREMIUM VOICE. The guess-and-reveal loop drives every post: ask an honest question, give the viewer time to guess, then close the loop in the same film. The voice stays calm, sparse and gallery-like, so the visuals carry the awe. The signature line is "Guess before it ends." The brand line is "The universe, drawn in light."

bios.youtube_description:
Start at the Planck length, where known physics runs out, and keep doubling. How many doublings until you reach a galaxy? Guess before it ends.

Lumiera is science, drawn in light: physics, space, biology and math as short cinematic films, glowing on deep space. Each film asks one clear question and gives you time to guess. Then it acts out the answer: copies line up, counters climb, and the scale finally makes sense.

What you'll find here:
- Scale journeys, from the Planck length to the observable universe
- Life up close, from viruses to blood cells
- Space and light, from the Sun to the Milky Way
- Math you can watch happen

A new film every week. Every number is checked, every comparison is real, and no title promises more than the film delivers. If we get a number wrong, we pin the correction.

Lumiera, from lumière: light.

link_in_bio:
Set up one free "Start here" page in the same glow-on-dark style and use that one link on all three profiles. If the domain lumiera.science is free, register it and point it at the page. Until then, use a minimal Linktree or Beacons page. Keep it to four buttons, in this order:
(1) "Watch The Doubling": links to the YouTube Short.
(2) "The numbers": a plain sources page with the size used for each stop and where it comes from. Planck length 1.6 × 10⁻³⁵ m (CODATA 1.616 × 10⁻³⁵ m). Proton 1.6 fm as used in the film, which is 100 quintillion Planck lengths (state on the page that the measured charge diameter is about 1.68 fm). Hydrogen atom about 0.1 nm, virus about 100 nm, red blood cell about 7.5 µm, ant about 4 mm, person about 1.7 m, Everest 8,849 m, Earth 12,742 km, Sun about 1.39 million km, solar system about 60 AU across (Neptune's orbit), nearest star 4.24 light-years, Milky Way about 100,000 light-years, observable universe about 93 billion light-years. With these sizes every step rounds to the number in the video (the proton is 66.4, so 66). This page backs up the "rounded to whole doublings" line in the Shorts description.
(3) "Ask Lumiera a question": a short form. The answers feed future films and comment replies.
(4) Lumiera on TikTok, Instagram and YouTube.

Platform notes:
- TikTok: personal accounts usually can't show a clickable bio link until about 1,000 followers, so the TikTok bio is written to work without one. Add the link when it unlocks.
- YouTube: put the link in the channel's Links section, because links in Shorts descriptions are not clickable.

content_pillars.name: Scale · How big is that?
content_pillars.description: The signature series that The Doubling starts. Sizes, distances, durations and quantities too large or too small to feel are made visible one step at a time, with step chips, a climbing counter and copies of the previous thing lining up. Each film opens with a number the viewer guesses before the reveal. This is the most shareable pillar, so post it most often early on.
video_ideas: The Halving, the direct sequel. Start at you (doubling 116) and halve your way down. How many halvings until you're the size of a hydrogen atom? The answer is 34 (116 - 82), and it is still about 34 on unrounded values. Reuse the logo rings and close on 'Remember that.'

The Doubling: Time. Start at the Planck time (5.4 × 10⁻⁴⁴ s) and double up to the age of the universe, which takes about 202 doublings. Hook: space took 205. Will time take more or fewer? Stops include a camera flash, a heartbeat, a human life and the age of the Sun. Compute and source every stop before scripting.

Fold it 42 times. In theory, a 0.1 mm sheet of paper folded in half 42 times would be about 440,000 km thick, past the Moon's average distance of about 384,400 km. The glowing stack climbs one fold at a time, and one plain line says that real paper can't be folded that many times.

A million, a billion, a trillion seconds. Three glowing clocks run to about 11.6 days, about 31.7 years and about 31,700 years. Viewers guess where each one lands. The third clock is still running when the film ends.

content_pillars.name: Cosmos & Light · How far, how fast?
content_pillars.description: Space and the physics of light. This pillar carries the name (lumière) most directly: how light travels, scatters and interferes, and where things really sit in the sky. Each film is built on one precise image, and honest qualifiers such as 'observable' and 'on average' stay in.
video_ideas: Sunlight, in transit. One photon leaves the Sun's surface while a timer runs, and it reaches Earth about 8 minutes 20 seconds later on average. Viewers guess the time before it lands. The sunlight on your face is already that old.
If space is full of stars, why is the night sky dark? Olbers' paradox: the sky fills with stars that should make it blaze, then the universe's finite age and light's finite speed leave it dark.
One photon at a time. Light passes through two slits one photon at a time. Each photon lands as a single random dot while a counter climbs, and the dots slowly build an interference pattern.

Do all the planets fit between Earth and the Moon? The honest answer depends on how you measure: center to center or surface to surface, mean or equatorial diameters. Show each version as it plays out. The point is precision, not a viral 'yes'.

content_pillars.name: Life, Measured · How many of you?
content_pillars.description: Biology at its true scale. Cells, DNA, blood and growth are counted and laid out the way The Doubling laid out the virus, the red blood cell and the ant, so the body becomes a landscape of real numbers. Estimate ranges are shown honestly.
video_ideas: Counting you. An adult body holds roughly 30 trillion human cells, and most of them are red blood cells. Viewers guess the total before the counter finishes filling a silhouette by cell type. It links back to the red blood cell at step 99.

Your DNA, unspooled. The DNA in one of your cells, stretched end to end, is about 2 meters long, packed into a nucleus a few micrometers across. The glowing strand unwinds next to a person-height marker.

One bacterium, doubling. Under ideal lab conditions E. coli can divide about every 20 minutes. The colony doubles on a counter, then the film shows why real growth stops: food runs out, waste builds up and space fills.

content_pillars.name: Pure Patterns · Why does that work?
content_pillars.description: Math made visible. Probability, geometry and number patterns are drawn as light, so an abstract result becomes something you watch happen and can check for yourself. Each film has one surprising answer.
video_ideas: The birthday threads. People appear one by one, and a thread of light joins every possible pair. Viewers guess the room size first. At 23 people there are 253 pairs, and the chance of a shared birthday passes 50% (about 50.7%).

The chessboard and the rice. One grain goes on the first square, and the count doubles on every square after. The counter races to 18,446,744,073,709,551,615 grains (2⁶⁴ − 1) on the full board: The Doubling's idea in 64 steps.
Pi from falling light. Random points of light fall into a square with a circle inside it. The share landing inside the circle, times 4, settles toward 3.14159… as a counter climbs.
Draw anything with spinning circles. A Fourier series is built one glowing circle at a time until the chain traces the Lumiera logo: a glowing dot with rings that double in radius.

voice_rules: Open with an honest question the viewer can answer in their head, and close that loop in the same video. Never hold the answer back for a 'part 2' or a follow.
Give the guess room to happen: ask, then let the counter run. 'Guess before it ends.' is the house signature for hooks, bios, captions and pinned comments.

Numbers are sacred. Check every figure against a source and keep it identical across the video, caption, title and comments. Use 'about' or '~' when rounding, never round in the direction that sounds more impressive, and list the sizes used in the description.
Keep the precise qualifiers: 'observable universe', 'where known physics runs out', 'on average', 'in theory'. Flag any simplification in one plain line.

Calm, precise, awe-filled. Write short declarative sentences, mostly in the present tense, and let the scale do the shouting. Never use 'mind-blowing', 'insane', 'you won't believe' or 'wait for it', fake urgency, or exclamation marks.
Comment prompts must have a real answer. Ask for a guess, a prediction or the next thing to measure. Never use 'only 1% get this' or tease something the video doesn't deliver.
Put the viewer on the scale, sparingly. 'You' is the measuring stick ('Doubling 116. Remember that.'), not someone to shout at. Address the viewer at most once or twice per caption.

Gallery typography. Use sentence case everywhere except profile names, step chips and end cards, and use '·' and line breaks as punctuation. Use at most one ✦ per text (the house mark) and ↓ only as a pointer to a link. No marks in titles or on-screen text.
Correct in public. If a number is wrong, pin a short correction with the right figure and a source and thank whoever caught it. Never argue and never delete.
rationale:
This set follows the judges' field winners and fixes every problem they listed. A final verification pass (October 2026) checked every platform limit against current sources, recounted every field in Python with len() (UTF-16 counts are the same) and recomputed every number.

What came from which candidate:
- Tagline: B's 'The universe, drawn in light.' (29 characters) is the brand line. A's 'Guess before it ends.' is the recurring engagement line.
- Display names: one separator ('·') is used everywhere, fixing C's mix of '|' and '·'. Each name carries search keywords, which neither judge got from B's bare 'Lumiera'.
- YouTube channel description: A's hook question now sits in the first 150 characters, followed by B's 'drawn in light' framing, A's list of what the channel covers, the cadence line, the trust promise and B's public-correction promise. It ends on the lumière origin.
- Captions: the TikTok caption is B's text with C's up-front figure and a comment ask. The Instagram caption is B's stops ladder plus C's share line, with one mark (✦). The YouTube title is A's: keyword first, a challenge, sentence case. The Shorts description is B's 13-stop list with '??? · the Milky Way (your guess)'.
- Content pillars: B's pillars with checked figures are the base. A's Halving, C's chessboard and C's Fourier logo are added. Each pillar name pairs B's name with a question-style series line, as judge 1 asked.
- Voice rules: A's loop and comment rules, plus B's 'never round toward impressive' and 'correct in public', plus C's sources page.

Fixes:
- Hashtags are cut to 5 on both TikTok and Instagram. Instagram announced a universal cap of 5 per post and Reel in December 2025 (socialmediatoday.com/news/instagram-implements-new-limits-on-hashtag-use/808309/). The ambiguous #scale is dropped.
- The pinned comment is 126 characters, under TikTok's 150-character comment limit, and carries A's 116 callback.
- Wherever the copy describes the end of the scale, it says 'observable universe'. The video's own end card, 'the edge of everything', is quoted only as on-screen text.
- C's exclamation marks, 'Come get curious!', 'brain feel bigger' line and title case are gone.
- The new-account title problem is fixed: the title no longer leads with 'The Doubling'.
- B's 'nearest whole doubling' claim is replaced. The description now says step numbers are 'rounded to whole doublings, using the sizes listed on the sources page'. The link-in-bio plan lists those sizes. With 1.6 fm the proton is 66.4, so 66.
- The weak backups lumiera.sci, lumiera.studio and thelumiera are dropped.
- The TikTok bio works without a link.
- The answer (185) is kept out of every caption, title, description, pinned comment and cover. It appears only in the alt text, for accessibility.

Fixes from the verification pass:
- Instagram name: cut from 44 to 25 characters ('Lumiera · Science & Space'). Instagram doesn't publish this limit. Most guides give 30 and a few give 64, so the set uses a value that is safe under both. If the app accepts the longer 'Lumiera · Science, Space & Physics Explained' (44), it is an optional upgrade, but decide before setting the name, because Instagram allows only two name changes in 14 days.
- Primary handle: changed from lumiera.science to lumiera_science. YouTube's handle rules say a handle must not be URL-like (support.google.com/youtube/answer/11585688), and lumiera.science is a real domain (the link plan even registers it). lumiera_science passes all three platforms' rules, so one handle works everywhere. The backups (lumierascience, lumiera.explained, lumiera_explained) do too.
- Voice rules: the marks rule now allows one ✦ plus ↓ as a link pointer, matching the Instagram bio, and the sentence-case rule now exempts profile names.
- Sources page: the proton entry now says 1.6 fm is the film's value (100 quintillion Planck lengths). The measured charge diameter is about 1.68 fm, which gives about 66.5 doublings, right on the 66/67 line, so the page states openly which size the film uses.
- Two slips in this rationale's working were corrected: the Halving uses 82.37 for hydrogen, not 82.45, and a trillion seconds is 31,688 years, not 31,686. The pillar copy was already right.

Numbers checked:
- All 13 stops, using log2(size / 1.6e-35 m): 66.4, 82.4, 92.3, 98.6, 107.6, 116.4, 128.7, 139.2, 146.0, 158.6, 170.7, 185.3, 205.1. The rounding is the same with the CODATA Planck length of 1.616 × 10⁻³⁵ m.
- Comparisons: 62,500 (about 60,000) protons per atom, 1,000 atoms per virus, 75 viruses per blood cell, 533 cells per ant, 425 ants per person, 5,205 people per Everest, 1,440 Everests per Earth, 109 Earths per Sun, 6,445 Suns per solar system, 4,469 solar systems to the nearest star, 23,585 trips to the Milky Way, 930,000 Milky Ways.
- 116 doublings up to you, 69 more to the galaxy (185), 20 more to the observable universe (205).
- The Halving: 116.35 - 82.37 = 33.98, so about 34.
- Planck time to the age of the universe: 202.3 doublings.
- Paper folded 42 times: 2^42 × 0.1 mm = 439,805 km.
- Chessboard: 2^64 − 1 = 18,446,744,073,709,551,615.
- Birthday problem: 23 people give 253 pairs and a 50.7% chance.
- Seconds: a million is 11.57 days, a billion 31.7 years, a trillion 31,688 years.
- Sunlight takes 499 s to reach Earth, about 8 min 20 s.

Character counts (conservative limits in brackets):
- Tagline 29.
- Handles 14 to 17 characters: lowercase letters, at most one period or underscore, never at the start or end. Valid for TikTok (24 max), Instagram (30) and YouTube (3 to 30, not URL-like).
- TikTok name 27/30. Instagram name 25/30. YouTube name 36/50.
- TikTok bio 70/80. Instagram bio 129/150. YouTube channel description 841/1,000.
- Shorts title 58/100. TikTok caption 203, or 264 with hashtags (2,200). Instagram caption 359, or 434 with hashtags (2,200). Alt text 753 (1,000). Shorts description 663/5,000.
- Pinned comment 126/150. Cover headline 31 characters, 6 words. YouTube tags: 15 tags with 190 characters of text, 226 counting commas and the quotes YouTube adds around multi-word tags (500).

Handle plan:
- Try bare 'lumiera' first, and use it only if it is free on all three platforms that day.
- Otherwise use lumiera_science everywhere. It carries the niche keyword and matches the lumiera.science site name.
- Keep lumiera.science for the website, not as a handle.
- If lumiera_science is taken anywhere, move all three platforms to the first backup that is free everywhere: lumierascience, lumiera.explained, lumiera_explained. Also register lumierascience defensively.

Check before posting:
- 'New film weekly' / 'A new film every week' appears in the Instagram bio, the YouTube channel description and the Shorts description. Change all three if the real posting schedule differs.
- Instagram's custom alt-text field may not exist for Reels (Meta's API supports custom alt text only on images). If it is missing, use the alt text on the cover image or a carousel version and turn on auto-captions. Do not move 185 into the caption.
- Instagram limits how often the name can be changed, so set it once.
- The TikTok 5-hashtag cap is reported rather than officially documented. Five tags is safe either way.
- Most guides give TikTok's bio limit as 80, and a few report 160 on some accounts. The 70-character bio fits either way.
- The .science domain ending has historically appeared on spam-abuse lists. Check that a lumiera.science link isn't flagged by the platforms before using it as the bio link.
